questions.q: What does it mean for a receipt to be 'on account' rather than applied?
options: The receipt has been matched to a specific invoice
The receipt has been recorded as received but not yet matched to any invoice
The receipt has bounced
The receipt has been refunded to the customer
questions.explain: A receipt sitting on account is recorded as cash received, but has not yet been applied against any specific invoice balance.

questions.q: Why does a single misapplied receipt create two incorrect balances rather than one?
options: The invoice that was actually paid still shows an open balance, while the invoice it was wrongly applied to appears paid when it wasn't
It doesn't — only the correct invoice is affected
It duplicates the cash in the bank account
It only affects the customer's credit limit
questions.explain: Because the payment reduced the wrong invoice's balance, the correctly-intended invoice remains open while an unrelated invoice incorrectly appears paid.

questions.q: How was it confirmed that the receipt was truly intended for INV-9042 rather than INV-9039?
options: The customer's guess over the phone
Both invoices had identical amounts
Oracle automatically flags the correct invoice
The remittance advice attached to the original payment explicitly referenced INV-9042's invoice number
questions.explain: The remittance advice attached to the payment explicitly named INV-9042, confirming the clerk's original application to INV-9039 was a mis-keying.

questions.q: What is the correct way to fix a receipt applied to the wrong invoice?
options: Delete the receipt and ask the customer to pay again
Leave it as is since the total cash received is still correct
Unapply it from the wrong invoice, then apply it correctly to the right invoice, preserving the application history
Manually edit the GL journal to fix the balances
questions.explain: Unapplying and reapplying correctly restores both invoices' balances while preserving the full history of what happened and when it was corrected.

questions.q: Besides correcting the two invoice balances, what else should be checked before closing this kind of ticket?
options: Nothing else is relevant once the balances are corrected
Whether a customer statement or dunning notice already went out reflecting the wrong balances
Whether the customer's tax ID is correct
Whether the bank reconciliation report needs to be deleted
questions.explain: A misapplied receipt can have downstream effects, such as an incorrect customer statement or an unwarranted dunning notice, that should be checked and addressed.
